MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 27, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on June 27, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 23, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

CS2. Conference With Legal Counsel: Consideration of Initiation of Litigation Pursuant
  to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: One Case, Adverse to State of
  California; and Pending Litigation: City of Mission Viejo v. State of California (DOF)

City Council Minutes  1  June 27, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received information and gave input but no
action was taken on either Closed Session item.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim July 2017 To Be National Parks and Recreation Month

  Mayor Bucknum presented the proclamation to Mark Nix, Director of Recreation and
  Community Services.

P2.  Proclamation June 2017 To Be Hunger Awareness Month

  Mayor Bucknum presented the proclamation to Jason Hatcher, Food Sourcing Manager for
  the Second Harvest Food Bank of Orange County.

P3.  Presentation on the Orange County District Attorney’s Efforts to Combat Human
  Exploitation and Trafficking

  The City Council received the presentation from Orange County District Attorney Tony
  Rackauckas.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: addressed the City Attorney's comments at the June 13, 2017, City Council
Meeting.

Julie Collier, Congressman Darrell Issa's Office: thanked the City for its support and inquired
about holding office hours at Mission Viejo City Hall.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar outlined below.

City Council Minutes  2  June 27, 2017
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of June 13, 2017, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated June 2, 2017 in the Amount of $1,081,623.67

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated June 9, 2017 in the Amount of $2,286,394.95

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Request for a one-time exemption to the “Vendor Permit Requirement” for food
  truck vendors at the annual Symphony in the Cities event and Concert on the Green.

  Approved the request for a one-time exemption to the “Vendor Permit Requirement” for
  food truck vendors at the Symphony in the Cities and Concert on the Green city events
  held on July 21 and 22, 2017.

6.  Consultant Services to Produce, Direct and Cablecast Live City Council Meetings for
  Television and the Web

  (1) Awarded a contract for the subject services to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2017,
  through June 30, 2019, in the amount of $46,913.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a
  purchase order to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2017, through June 30, 2018, in an
  amount not to exceed $22,911 pending adoption of the 2017-2019 budget by the City
  Council.

7.  Consultant Services for Coordination of Activities at Mission Viejo Television
  (MVTV)

  (1) Awarded a contract to Eric Winter for coordination of activities at Mission Viejo
  Television for the period of July 1, 2017, through June 30, 2019, in the amount of $56,195;
  and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Eric Winter for the period of July 1,
City Council Minutes  3  June 27, 2017
   2017, through June 30, 2018, in the amount of $27,750 pending adoption of the Fiscal Year
  2017-2019 budget by the City Council.

8.  Consultant Services for Producer/Director of Various Mission Viejo Television
  (MVTV) Programs

  (1) Awarded a contract for the subject services to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2017,
  through June 30, 2019, in the amount of $120,646; and (2) authorized issuance of a
  purchase order to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2017, through June 30, 2018, in an
  amount not to exceed $60,278.00 pending adoption of the 2017-2019 budget by the City
  Council.

9.  Agreement to Provide Disaster-Related Debris Removal and Recovery Services.

  (1) Authorized the City Manager to Execute the Agreement with Ashbritt, Inc. to provide
  Disaster-Related Debris Removal and Recovery Services; and (2) executed the County of
  Orange Indemnification Supplement.

10.  Fee Waiver for Temporary Promotional Sign Permit

  Approved Two-Year Fee Waiver for Temporary Promotional Sign Permit to June 30, 2019.

11.  Amendment to Agreement for Building Plan Check and Inspection Services - Charles
  Abbott Associates, Inc.

  Approved the First Amendment of Agreement with Charles Abbott Associates, Inc. for
  Building Plan Check and Inspection Services for the Period from July 1, 2017, to June 30,
  2019.

12.  Agreement for Professional Services for Housing Rehabilitation Program - Housing
  Rehabilitation Consulting Services (HRCS)

  Approved Agreement with HRCS from July 1, 2017 to June 30, 2019, in an amount not to
  exceed $114,500 ($57,250 /year) for Technical Assistance.

13.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Alarcon to Santa Margarita
  Parkway - (CIP 229)

  (1) Awarded contract to Horizon Construction Company International, Inc. for the
  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Alarcon to Santa Margarita Parkway-
  (CIP 229), in an amount not to exceed $605,265; and (2) adopted Resolution 17-26
  Amending the Fiscal Year 2016-2017 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement
  Project 229.

14.  Annual Routine Street Sweeping Services

City Council Minutes  4  June 27, 2017
   (1) Approved the Third Amendment with Sunset Property Services for the period of July
  1, 2017 through June 30, 2018 in the amount of $355,941.76; and (2) authorized staff to
  issue a purchase order to Sunset Property Services for the period of July 1, 2017, through
  June 30, 2018, in an amount not to exceed $355,941.76 pending adoption of the Fiscal Year
  2017-2019 budget by the City Council.

15.  Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement Project (TRAP)

  Adopted Resolution 17-27 Authorizing the Director of Public Works to Apply for Funds
  for the Environmental Cleanup, Tier 1 Grant Program Under Orange County Local
  Transportation Ordinance No. 3 for the Mission Viejo Trash and Runoff Abatement
  Projects

16.  2017 Residential Resurfacing—CDBG Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP
  17838)—Award of Contract

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to All American Asphalt in the
  amount of $1,589,305.00.

17.  Establish an Appropriations Limit for the 2017-18 Fiscal Year

  Adopted Resolution 17-28 Establishing an Appropriations Limit for the 2017-18 Fiscal
  Year.

18.  Traffic Signal Maintenance-Contract Change Order 2

  Approved Contract Change Order 2 to Contract A15-54 with Computer Service Company
  in an amount not to exceed $75,000.00.

19.  Microsoft Licensing Renewal

  Approved purchase order for year three of three-year agreement with Microsoft for
  Microsoft Product Licensing renewal and issue a purchase order to SoftwareONE
  (Formerly CompuCom) for such services for 2017-18 in the amount of $71,517.28.

21.  Upgrades to Building Access Control for City Facilities

  Approved entering into agreement and issuance of purchase order to RD Systems, Inc., in
  the amount of $103,580.83 for purchase and implementation of building access control
  system components and alarms.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

20.  Document Management System Software and Hardware Upgrade

  By consensus, the City Council delayed this matter to the meeting of July 11, 2017.
City Council Minutes  5  June 27, 2017
 OLD BUSINESS

22.  Recommended Name for the Wall of Recognition Display

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report and
  answered the City Council Members’ questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to approve the
  addition of Sharon Cody for the Wall of Recognition Display.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

23.  Adoption of the 2017-19 Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: spoke in favor of budgeting for computer upgrades rather than having
  the money sit in the reserve fund.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to approve
  Resolution 17-30 Adopting a Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for 2017-19 and
  Appropriating Funds for FY 17/18 Only.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

24.  FY 2017-18 Law Enforcement Services Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented staff report.

  Mayor Bucknum asked for clarification regarding the First Responders helicopters and how
  the overlap is handled with the Orange County Fire Authority in the contract.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to (1)
  approve the FY 2017-18 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange
  for an amount not to exceed $19,041,089; and (2) authorize the City Manager to approve
  reimbursements related to special enforcement services in an amount not to exceed $35,000
  for FY 2017-18.
City Council Minutes  6  June 27, 2017
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

25.  Eleventh Amendment to City Manager Employment Agreement

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: spoke against the City Manager’s employment agreement.

  Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Council Member Kelley, (1) adopt
  Resolution 17-31 Amending the City's Salary Schedule and Establishing Salary Ranges
  for Authorized Job Classifications; and (2) adopt Resolution 17-32 Approving the
  Eleventh Amendment to the City Manager Employment Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

26.  Alternatives to the City’s Insurance Programs

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  authorize the City Manager to give immediate notice of Intent to Withdraw from the
  California Joint Powers Insurance Authority (CJPIA) Joint Powers Agreement and related
  Joint Protection Programs.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

27.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

City Council Minutes  7  June 27, 2017
 28.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

29.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update

  Battalion Chief Shane Sherwood reported on the current fire season and that OCFA has
  assisted with fires in other areas within the state. He recapped the recent Water Safety
  Program at Montanoso Recreation Center and spoke about the ABC’s of drowning. Lastly,
  Chief Sherwood invited the Council to attend the graduation of OCFA Academy 44 which
  will advance 24 new firefighters.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

30.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell discussed his attendance at the Orange County Metropolitan Water
District Annual Water Summit where he learned about the needs of the local water system as well
as statewide needs. He said The Delta Stewardship Council is planning a long term view to the
year 2100 and the conveyance of water from Northern to Southern California is a huge issue. The
state levee system is in need of an approximately $5 billion dollar investment and many of the
levees are over 100 years old and privately owned. Council Member Goodell said that due to
environmental effects of the delta smelt fish, this year alone a 15-year supply of water from the
Sierra Nevada has been flushed to the ocean and not captured and there are 1,250 California dams
that are over 50 to 100 years old and need repairs. Council Member Goodell discussed his
attendance at the Chamber of Commerce breakfast, the 23rd Annual DAWG Walk, the Republican
Party’s annual Flag Salute at the Hotel Irvine and announced that he will be attending the League
of California Cities training later this week.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the State of South Orange County presentation
put on by County Supervisor Lisa Bartlett and she thanked the Supervisor for providing a wealth
of information and for the hard work she is doing for South Orange County. Council Member
Kelley also attended the recent DAWG Walk and she thanked Sharon Cody for the work she has
done for the DAWG program as well as the many dedicated volunteers. She further discussed her
attendance, with her three grandsons, at the Water Safety Program at Montanoso Recreation Center
and she commended staff member Mark Thorndyke for his water safety presentation. Council
City Council Minutes  8  June 27, 2017
 Member Kelley reminded residents of the 4th of July Street Faire and thanked the Mission Viejo
Activities Committee for their hard work putting this event together every year. She also
announced that on Sunday July 16 from 4:00 to 7:00 p.m., Boots Beer and Barbecue will be held
at the Norman P. Murray Community Center to raise funds for the City’s adopted Marine Battalion.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that he too attended the State of South Orange County
presentation by Supervisor Bartlett and he said that she is doing a wonderful job. He noted that
Supervisor Bartlett recently nominated him to be on the Veterans Advisory Council for Orange
County and he is hoping that the other Supervisors support him for that role. Council Member
Raths wished the City’s Economic Development Liaison, Karen Wylie, all the best in her
retirement.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Following up on the Fire Chief’s drowning presentation, Mayor Pro Tem Sachs stated that after
kids, the next highest incident of drowning occurs in seniors. He announced that the budget for
the next two years is in good shape but he expressed concern that the financial master plan points
out that at some point expenditures will out-pace revenues. He spoke about the legislation on
prevailing wages, the increase in the minimum wage which has adverse effects on cities, and said
he is concerned about pension liabilities. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs suggested that the City start
looking into the future to plan how it will continue funding the many programs it offers to residents.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum highlighted Consent Calendar item #10 which is a fee waiver program for
temporary sign permits to benefit the City’s businesses. She said that the Economic Development
Committee is working closely with the business community and she highlighted the upcoming
Chamber of Commerce “Restaurant Week” August 21-27, 2017. Mayor Bucknum announced that
Saddleback Church has a volunteer group for the prevention of human trafficking. She also invited
residents to the Fourth of July Street Faire and announced that she attended the Mission Viejo High
School Graduation where she made a presentation to the school on their 50-year Anniversary and
the 50th graduating class of 2017.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:37 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, July 11, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

____________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 11, 2017

City Council Minutes  9  June 27, 2017
